fourFullPromptAnswerNoteAssessments.plausibility: A genuine paper-staining phenomenon associated with water exposure, not the exact scattered-spot glossary label.
fourFullPromptAnswerNoteAssessments.truthUniqueKey: LOC FEDLINK glossary explicitly defines foxing as a descriptive term for scattered paper spots commonly reddish-brown but ranging yellow to black. Its uncertain multiple possible causes mean this is not a unique biological diagnosis. Water tide lines follow wetting/staining; iron-gall corrosion follows ink lines; mold may produce staining/foxing, but is not the descriptive term requested by this precise glossary entry. Unique key is foxing, independent of frozen slot.

The note accurately connects water exposure and degradation-dependent severity.
